decisions.reason: The question asks whether highlighting helps users spot where to edit, but it does not ask whether highlighting likely edits works better than highlighting low-probability tokens.
The method describes what the edit model predicts but omits the preliminary data from nine coders who corrected Codex outputs until the tasks were completed properly.

The poster gives the sample size and the number and difficulty of the LeetCode tasks. It omits the employer context, participants’ Python experience, and randomization of task order and tool-to-task assignments.
The poster identifies the shared model, all three conditions, and both thresholds. It omits that the thresholds were chosen to match total highlight counts across the three tasks.
The results give all three means and both p-values with the correct comparisons. Panel (a)’s caption states the 10-minute cap.
Panel (b) shows the expected survival pattern, but the poster does not state the exact rates, define survival as a token remaining untouched, or connect the pattern to more localized editing.
Panel (c) shows higher preference for Edit model highlights on a scale extending to 7. The poster omits the exact means, p-value, item topics, and reverse coding of distraction.
The poster omits that the edit model was trained on the evaluated completions and that comparable effects on unseen tasks remain unverified.
The poster omits that effects on oversight accuracy and automation bias remain untested.

notes: The figure caption correctly maps panels (a), (b), and (c). The small axis labels, condition labels, and legend need enlargement for comfortable reading. Exact values in panels (b) and (c) cannot be verified from bar heights at this resolution. The title, section headings, and figure placement make the reading order clear. This review is based on the supplied export and editable text.
